chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'When does a man shorten his prayer when he intends to travel?' He said: 'When he departs from the houses.' I said: 'What if a man intends to travel and leaves when the sun declines (for Dhuhr)?' He said: 'When you leave, pray two rak'ahs.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And it is not permissible for anyone to fast voluntarily or obligatorily while traveling, except the fasting of three days of blood-expiation from the total of the ten days. This is indicated by what he narrated:'
ai.seo_question: When does a traveler begin shortening their prayers and are they required to fast while traveling?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the precise moment the travel status (*safar*) begins for prayer shortening, defining it as the point when the traveler is concealed from the city's buildings, a criterion often interpreted as leaving the built-up area. It further establishes the general principle that travelers are exempt from both obligatory and voluntary fasting, with the specific exception of the three days of blood-money (*dam*) fasts required for Hajj al-Tamattu', highlighting the flexibility (*rukhsah*) granted in Shia jurisprudence for ease during travel.
